issue_request: FHIR-27802 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the secpriv-module #user section. It asked to distinguish application users and roles from Practitioner/PractitionerRole, noting that generic user and role management is typically outside FHIR, that PractitionerRole may be relevant for practitioner users, and that users can also be Patient or RelatedPerson rather than Practitioner.
initial_application: The prior FHIR-27802 application was commit b1ab4dabb8bd626b70ea00d24b50e4eec9431b5f, which added the general-IT/SCIM and practitioner-user sentences to source/secpriv-module.html. The current source still misspelled PractitionerRole as PractionerRole and did not carry over the Jira resolution's Patient/RelatedPerson clarification.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread supports the distinction: Lloyd McKenzie said generic user, user role, and permission management belongs outside FHIR, Practitioner is for people in a professional capacity, and Practitioner should not be used to represent Patient or RelatedPerson users. source/hierarchy.xml lists secpriv-module.html as the Security and Privacy page, confirming build scope. A later security spelling issue, FHIR-55342, fixed an unrelated contraction and did not address this wording.
reconciliation: Updated source/secpriv-module.html to spell PractitionerRole correctly and add a sentence clarifying that Practitioner and PractitionerRole are not the only possible FHIR linkages for user identity; patient and related-person users link to Patient or RelatedPerson as appropriate.
